title: Even the attackers leave the door open
subtitle: Eight stolen certificate keys, a PHP fix that leaked early, and ransomware crews whose AI agent logs sat on an open server
editor_note: Today's thread is open doors. Eight eMudhra intermediate keys that browsers trusted for any site were compromised, and Chrome and Firefox had to shut them out within hours. PHP is rushing out fixes because details leaked before the embargo. Then the twist: ransomware affiliates who ran Claude and Kimi through a coding agent left their own session logs on an open server, and that is how SOCRadar learned they beat refusals by calling the work red-teaming. In Japan, a broker saw fraudulent trades go through. Further out, the open door is a good thing: mathematicians argue over an AI proof, a bank rule pushes credit somewhere new, and a 3,400-year-old archive opens up. This edition replaces the 02:00 JST draft with a full morning scan.

sections.headline: Eight keys that could vouch for any website were stolen
sections.deck: Compromised eMudhra intermediate CA keys sent Chrome, Firefox, Go and NSS into same-day fixes. Chrome found no rogue certificates in CT logs.
sections.why: Your agents and containers trust bundled CA stores; the fix only reaches you when you update them.

sections.deck: What moved in your stack overnight.

sections.headline: Patches, betas and one bad region

items.headline: PHP readies emergency fixes for two critical flaws
items.note: PHP says CVSS 9.2; watchTowr says 10.0 and RCE across PHP 5 to 8. Details leaked early; no known exploitation yet.

items.headline: Google Cloud's London region spiked in connection failures
items.note: Cloudflare Radar saw it from outside from 06:00 UTC; posts tied Revolut and UK bank outages to it.

items.headline: TypeScript 7.1 Beta adds a preview API
items.note: The native compiler gets content mappers and a preview API for tool authors.

items.headline: durable-harness lets any coding agent survive a crash
items.note: Pi, OpenCode, Codex or Claude Code sessions resume after failures, on Vercel, Postgres or a laptop.

items.headline: uv check: type-check a Python project in one command
items.note: Experimental: installs ty, syncs dependencies and checks the project with no config.

sections.deck: The one to read in full.

sections.headline: Ransomware crews ran AI agents, then left the logs open
sections.deck: SOCRadar found 8,000+ messages from INC and The Gentlemen affiliates using Claude and Kimi, plus 46 encryptor builds. The claims rest on the operators' own exposed records.
sections.why: You build agent safety tools; a fake red-team authorization is exactly the prompt your guards should catch.

sections.quote: To fight refusals, they authorized it by calling it red-teaming.

sections.deck: Everything you saved since the last issue.

sections.headline: Three saves: a fast site, a nightly audit, an open inference stack

items.note: The speed play: ship a template site onto a trending keyword before anyone else.
A loop worth stealing: let an agent audit yesterday's work every night and propose fixes.
DeepSeek's production inference engine is now open source, so the serving tricks behind its low prices are public.

sections.headline: Skills that collide, and search that needs no model

items.headline: Load two skills for one job and the model drops one
items.note: Rule-following fell from 93-99% to 61-62%. One shared closing example cut takeover to 1-15%.
items.why: Check your own skill folders for overlap; the worked example is the real spec.

items.headline: Zed tried 25 ways to search MCP tools and chose BM25
items.note: 150 queries, 536 tools; weighted BM25 won on speed with no model or API calls.

sections.deck: One step out: machines in mathematics and medicine.

sections.headline: An AI proof lands, and some mathematicians step back
sections.verdict: Both are true at once: the strongest AI result in mathematics so far, and a pledge to keep AI out of research. The dispute is about method and credit, not whether the proof checks.

items.label: Quanta Magazine
items.note: Lichtman calls OpenAI's quasi-Riemann proof the most significant AI-for-math result yet.

items.label: New Scientist
items.note: About a thousand mathematicians pledge to avoid AI in their own research.

sections.headline: An AI-designed virus treats one patient

items.caption: Omnii-1, a genome model, designed bacteria-killing phages given under compassionate use. One case, the company's own account, covered by the NYT.
items.why: Same pattern as code agents: a model proposes, and clinicians decide whether to trust it.

sections.deck: Worth knowing, whatever you work on.

sections.headline: When banks pull back, who lends?
sections.verdict: The BIS paper finds that safer-bank liquidity rules moved lending outside banks; Nikkei shows the same shift starting in Japan as deposits stall.

items.label: BIS
items.note: Regions with more LCR-constrained banks saw stronger private credit growth.

items.headline: In 1934 a dictionary added 'thon', a pronoun that never caught on
items.why: The search for a singular gender-neutral pronoun is about a century old.

sections.headline: A good dog finds the sea vomit
sections.note: A black Labrador from the Scottish Highlands won an award for sniffing out the carpet sea squirt, an invasive species, along British waters.
